attempted_contrary_interfaces: First-tier diversity treated as independent lower-tier supply.
A complete document treated as operational capability.
A partial exposure or criterion input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Capacity, stock or staff double-counted for routine and contingency use.
Buyer savings treated as joint fair gain.

positive_controls.argument: A two-sided contract defining accepted requests, ownership and backpressure identifies the work boundary and refusal semantics needed to interpret or revise the admission rule.
An evidence-dependent commitment boundary and option-expiry date identify which work can remain provisional and which admission decision would harden the next investment.
Forecast ranges, observed completion and explicit external commitments inform the capacity and exception assumptions under which a particular release limit is defensible.
Supplier lead times, change responsibilities and real commercial authority identify which pre-entry preparation or exception the admission policy must consider.
The actual readiness conditions, support capacity and cutover authority specify which work may be admitted or held and what exceptional release requires.
Demonstrated recovery time, state-reconciliation limits and responder capacity constrain a release limit or exception for the same class of work.
Service obligations, maintenance horizons and end-of-support information determine work classes, priority and exceptions relevant to the maintenance admission rule.
The actual consequence and applicable control basis constrain which admission exceptions, preauthorization and evidence are legitimate for that work.
